delete.description: Permanently deletes a trading account owned by the authenticated user, along with its derived performance history (portfolio snapshots). Demo accounts are deleted together with everything that belongs to them (positions, transactions, snapshots). For non-demo accounts, refuses to delete an account that still has positions, or one that is referenced by a generated tax report — close the account instead to preserve that history. Ownership and retention checks run under the same account lock as participating trade/import writes and new tax-report references. Deletion cascades inactive opening drafts, draft cash operations and import batches; it does not confirm or activate accounting.

get.description: Returns exact ledger-replayed balances and effective-dated activity, the opening boundary, source freshness, unsupported events and attested statement evidence. Transfer audit command summaries include transfer.fromAccountId, transfer.toAccountId and fee (charged to this account only); the shared idempotency key and source reference identify the pair. Transfer principal contributes to account-level external capital and cancels across both endpoints; fees remain costs. Paired operation integrity is checked before returning balances. Active and archived real accounts are read-only here. Evidence is user-attested, not broker-verified; stale or unsupported source history is explicitly flagged.

No holdings, FX, activation, direct edits or one-sided reversals; corrections use the dedicated paired audit workflow. Same-key retries reuse both operations.

Same-key retries reuse the pair, even after later activity. No one-sided funding revision, holdings move or FX.

Positive exchanged amounts are before separately recorded fees, which may be in either exchanged currency; no third currency. One date/sequence links both currency legs atomically. Full dated funding, immutable history and exact retries are enforced. Principal and fees are not external capital. Revisions use the dedicated audited correction endpoint; no direct edits, holdings changes or account activation.

Split actions and effects are included in source fingerprints. Missing or inconsistent retained effects reject the preview rather than returning partial inventory. It cannot confirm or enable accounting; retained splits remain a blocking issue for opening confirmation and cash-completeness certification pending broader historical protections and release review. Missing funding is never invented. Limited to 5000 parcels, 500 import batches, 50000 transactions, 10000 relevant import events, 500 split actions and 50000 split effects; exceeding any limit returns 422.

post.description: Changes the live manual long BUY date, quantity, price and fees, recomputes parcel cost basis, remaining inventory and realized results, and appends an immutable cash revision with before/after source snapshots and fingerprint continuation. Sale quantities and allocations never change. The parcel must have exactly one BUY, cover all sales and precede their dates. Same-day sales require effective draft cash ordered after the acquisition. Imported parcels and broker-linked sales are excluded. Account, instrument, currency and source identity cannot change. The acquisition must stay after opening and within the original observation date. Quantity is an exact decimal string with at most 12 fractional digits, at most 9007199254740991, and must round-trip through the existing Float storage without changing decimal value. Gross consideration is quantity times price rounded half-up to 2 decimal places. Same-Sydney-date edits retain timestamps; changed dates use 01:00 UTC. The original opening and statement evidence remain unchanged; unrelated drafts and tax reports can become stale. No spendable cash or accounting activation is enabled.

Gross consideration is quantity times price rounded half-up to the transaction's two decimal places. A same-Sydney-date correction preserves the original timestamp; changing date records the new calendar date at 01:00 UTC. Dates must remain after opening, on/after acquisition and within the original observation date. Same-day sales must follow effective acquisition cash in explicit sequence order. The original opening snapshot and statement evidence never change; other drafts become stale. Expected revision/source and idempotency checks serialize edits. This changes live trade history and can make existing tax reports stale, but does not activate accounting or post spendable cash.

Reconciliation is bounded to 10000 imported executions and 50000 transactions.

Exact net income must equal acquisition consideration plus fees plus an explicit account-paid residual; issuer-held credits, extra funding, existing-receipt relinking and AMIT components are unsupported. Acquisition follows income in date/sequence order and, with validated split history, must follow the split date. Paired immutable links and full funded replay protect both records. Independent income revisions, acquisition corrections/voids and direct deletion are blocked; use the dedicated paired revision workflow. No activation or external capital is created.

No effective SELL may remain on the new parcel. Corrections update statement tax figures and acquisition/date/order/residual together, retain all slots and require funded replay; reversal removes the effective income and parcel without a disposal. Moving the acquisition later or reversing it must preserve historical holdings for other active income and reinvestment entitlements; review is limited to 500 distinct date/parcel checks. With validated split history, entitlement uses split-adjusted holdings. A pre-split correction must preserve the acquisition date and quantity; reverse dependent splits before changing either or reversing the reinvestment. Issuer-held credits and one-sided changes remain blocked. Exact retained retries survive later activity.

post.description: Without `eventIds`, applies the whole plan and returns 409 while blocking issues remain. With `eventIds`, applies only those events and returns 409 if an earlier event of the same asset is unresolved or not included. Runs in one database transaction, in chronological order. Locks the owned account, rechecks that it is active and non-demo, and verifies that events and eligible holdings still match the prepared plan before any trade writes. Concurrent changes return 409 and require reviewing a refreshed plan; the import is not silently reallocated. Parcel creation, allocated SELLs, recomputed results and event links commit or roll back together. No live cash postings or opening activation are performed.

patch.description: Crypto symbols must match the venue quote currency. Changing a Kraken instrument validates its market; unchanged historical instruments remain editable. Acquisition edits commit the BUY and recomputed parcel results together. Bought units cannot be reduced below already-sold units. Account moves lock both accounts in stable order and recheck the demo/real boundary. Inactive draft cash is not spent or activated. An edit or move that would leave open holdings in a closed account returns 409; reopen the account first. Corrections and moves of fully closed history remain allowed. Imported acquisition values and source identities cannot be changed here. Financial edits, instrument/account changes and deletion of cash-linked trades require coordinated correction and return 409 here, including for reversed cash operations. The opening reconciliation workflow supports manual acquisition and sale corrections, not deletion or moves. Notes and metadata remain editable; resubmitting unchanged financial values is allowed. Source-neutral metadata preserves the position's updatedAt for accounting fingerprint compatibility; financial changes continue to update it.

post.description: For an open long position with a stop loss that is not already flagged, decides whether the stop has been reached and, if so, persists stopLossHitAt so the flag survives the price recovering. If currentPrice is supplied and at or below the stop, the stop is flagged immediately. Otherwise daily lows are scanned from the time the stop was last set (or the open date, if never changed) to today; the first day whose low reached the stop becomes stopLossHitAt (day-granular). Editing the stop loss price clears the flag. Already-flagged, closed, short, or stop-less positions are returned unchanged. Saving rechecks the stop and holding inputs under user/account/parcel locks; concurrent changes return 409 rather than persisting a stale hit. Split-affected stop monitoring is unavailable and returns 409, including for previously flagged stops and retained reversed splits.

post.description: Computes a capital gains summary for the given Australian financial year across an explicit set of Trading Accounts (a "declaration"), renders a PDF, and stores it as a new revision for that (financial year, account selection) combination. Previous revisions are retained and stay downloadable so an already-lodged report is never overwritten. Regenerating with unchanged content returns the existing current revision instead of creating a new one. Dates in newly generated PDFs use dd/MM/yyyy; regenerating a report with the older date format creates a new revision without modifying the original PDF. New revisions lock selected accounts in stable ID order and recheck ownership and non-demo eligibility before storing account references. A concurrent deletion or report revision change fails explicitly instead of orphaning a new report. Report inputs are rechecked under those locks before returning or saving a revision; changed holdings, disposals or loss carry-forward require a retry.

delete.description: Marks the account deleted and revokes every session immediately. The data is retained until the grace period expires, during which signing in returns 403 with `accountPendingDeletion` and the account can be restored via POST /api/auth/restore. After that a scheduled purge removes the user and all their positions, accounts, snapshots, tax reports and watchlists. An exclusive user lock waits for participating financial writes before marking deletion and revoking sessions together. In-flight writes waiting behind deletion are refused even if their initial authentication check already succeeded.
